title: Cache Configuration
description: Learn how to configure Apollo Client cache settings for optimal performance and data consistency.

data.text: Apollo Client uses a normalized cache by default. Every object returned by a GraphQL query is stored by its `id` and `__typename`. When a subsequent query returns the same object, Apollo merges the fields automatically. Understanding this normalization is key to mastering Apollo caching.

data.definition:
graph TD
    A[GraphQL Response] --> B[Normalize by id/__typename]
    B --> C[Store in Cache]
    C --> D[Query A Returns Partial Data]
    C --> E[Query B Returns Same Object]
    D --> F[Merge Fields]
    E --> F
    F --> G[Complete Object in UI]
data.caption: Apollo normalized cache flow

data.title: Options
Cache configuration

data.text: Use `cache-and-network` during development to see both cached and fresh data. Use `cache-first` in production for fastest perceived performance.

data.takeaway: Understanding Apollo cache configuration is essential for building predictable data-driven UIs.
